textbookText: 117. The Mean Value Theorem states that for a function continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b), there exists a point c where: A) f'(c) equals the average rate of change [f(b) − f(a)]/(b − a) B) f(c) = 0 always C) f'(c) is always zero D) f(a) = f(b) necessarily

118. Which of these is an extraordinary real-world use of integration? A) Calculating the area under a demand curve in economics to determine consumer surplus B) Integration only applies to abstract mathematics with no economic or physical use C) Integration can only compute the derivative of a function, not area D) Integration is limited strictly to computing straight-line distances

119. L'Hôpital's Rule is used to evaluate limits of the indeterminate form: A) 0/0 or ∞/∞, by differentiating numerator and denominator separately B) Any limit, regardless of form, by squaring the function C) Only limits that already have a defined finite value D) Only limits involving trigonometric functions

120. The area between two curves y = f(x) and y = g(x) (where f(x) ≥ g(x)) from x=a to x=b is found by: A) ∫ₐᵇ [f(x) − g(x)] dx B) ∫ₐᵇ [f(x) + g(x)] dx C) f(b) − g(a) D) The product f(x)·g(x) integrated
